B.explanation: Maximum order is $n = 3$, so total maxima are $3$ on each side plus the central maximum, giving $7$.

hints: First convert 400 lines per millimetre into the grating spacing $d$ in metres using $d = 1/400 \text{ mm}$.
Recall $d\sin\theta = n\lambda$ for normal incidence, with $\lambda = 700 \text{ nm}$ and the largest possible order occurring at $\sin\theta = 1$.
Calculate $d/\lambda$ and round down to the integer order, then add the matching orders on both sides plus the $n = 0$ maximum.
walkthrough: Calculate the slit separation: $d = \frac{1.0 \times 10^{-3} \text{ m}}{400} = 2.5 \times 10^{-6} \text{ m}$.
Use the diffraction grating equation for normal incidence: $d\sin\theta = n\lambda$, where $\lambda = 700 \text{ nm} = 7.0 \times 10^{-7} \text{ m}$.
The highest order occurs at the largest angle $\theta = 90^{\circ}$, so $\sin\theta = 1$ and $n_{max} = d/\lambda$.
Substitute values: $n_{max} = \frac{2.5 \times 10^{-6} \text{ m}}{7.0 \times 10^{-7} \text{ m}} = 3.57$, so only integer orders $n = 0, 1, 2, 3$ are possible.
Count maxima on both sides of the centre: $3$ orders to the left, $3$ orders to the right, plus $1$ central $n = 0$ maximum gives $2 \times 3 + 1 = 7$. This is option B.
